name: rowWeightedMedians
title: Calculates the weighted medians for each row in a matrix

origin.description: Calculates the weighted medians for each row (column) in a matrix.
origin.usage:
rowWeightedMedians(x, w = NULL, rows = NULL, cols = NULL,
  na.rm = FALSE, ..., useNames = TRUE)

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length K (one weight per column).

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of rows to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: A vector indicating a subset of columns to operate over. If NULL, no subsetting is done.

arguments.name: na.rm
arguments.text: If TRUE, missing values are excluded.

arguments.name: useNames
arguments.text: If TRUE (default), names attributes of the result are set, otherwise not.

origin.details: If no weights are given, rowMedians() is used. Otherwise each row is passed to weightedMedian() after base-R subscripting. A negative weight is an error. A zero weight is kept for that call, which drops it. A missing weight makes the row NA when na.rm is false.
origin.value: A numeric vector of length N (one value for each selected row).

translation.description: Calculates the weighted medians for each row (column) in a matrix.
translation.usage:
rowWeightedMedians(x, w=None, rows=None, cols=None, na_rm=False,
  use_names=True, interpolate=None, ties=None, idxs=None)

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An N by K array. Axis 0 is rows and axis 1 is columns, matching the printed R matrix. A one-dimensional sequence is rejected.

arguments.name: w
arguments.text: A numeric vector of length K, one weight per column. None uses the unweighted median. A negative weight, including negative infinity, is an error before any row is reduced. Zero and negative zero are passed on and dropped by weightedMedian. A missing weight makes every row missing when na_rm is false, and is dropped when na_rm is true.

arguments.name: rows
arguments.text: 1-based rows to include. None uses every row. Zero is dropped, a positive index keeps its place and may repeat, and a negative index drops that row. A missing index inserts a missing row.

arguments.name: cols
arguments.text: 1-based columns to include. None uses every column. w is subset with this same index after its length has been checked against the original matrix.

arguments.name: na_rm
arguments.text: If True, missing values in a row are excluded, and a missing weight is dropped. This is na.rm. The default is False.

arguments.name: use_names
arguments.text: Accepted for compatibility with useNames. The result is always a plain float64 vector; names are not attached.

arguments.name: interpolate
arguments.text: Passed to weightedMedian when w is given. None follows that function: true when ties is omitted, false when ties is given. Ignored when w is None.

arguments.name: ties
arguments.text: Passed to weightedMedian when w is given. "min", "max", "mean", or "weighted". A positive infinite weight ignores ties. Ignored when w is None.

arguments.name: idxs
arguments.text: 1-based index forwarded to weightedMedian for each row, after rows and cols have been applied. None uses the whole row. Ignored when w is None.

translation.details: With weights, each selected row is passed to weightedMedian together with w, na_rm, interpolate, ties, and idxs. Non-positive weights that survive the negative check are dropped there. A positive infinite weight uses that function's partial-sort median and ignores ties. With no weights, the result follows rowMedians: an even count averages the two central values, a missing value with na_rm false is R's NA, and a margin with nothing left is plain NaN. The weighted call on an empty row is R's NA instead.
translation.value: A float64 vector of length N, one value for each selected row.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from matrixstats.rowweightedmedians import rowWeightedMedians

x = np.array([[1.0, 5.0, 9.0], [2.0, 6.0, 10.0], [3.0, 7.0, 11.0], [4.0, 8.0, 12.0]])
rowWeightedMedians(x, w=np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]))
